# Visuals reference

Every class in `assets/scripts/visuals/`, from its doc comments. The overview is in [README.md](README.md).

- [FloatingSword](#floatingsword)
- [ToyWaddle](#toywaddle)

## FloatingSword

`res://assets/scripts/visuals/FloatingSword.gd`, extends [`Node3D`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node3d.html)

A sword that floats beside the pawn and swings through each attack, exactly where the hit is checked.

The owner's toy look (pawn spec 8.12): the pawn doesn't hold it; it hovers at its right side like a toy waved next to a figure, and swoops through the swing. Put it under the pawn's Visual (not Model, which rocks with the waddle). It makes the sword itself from `sword_scene`.

What it shows, frame by frame:
- Hovering: at the pawn's side, about chest high, blade up, bobbing and swaying gently.
- A swing (any MeleeAttackAbility on the pawn that's running), through its phases (MeleeAttackAbility.swing_phase, from its steps): windup, it swings back to just behind where the hit starts; hit, it sweeps through the hit, blade pointing out from the pawn's chest through each spot the hit checks (MeleeAttackAbility.hit_offset_at, the same path the hits use), edge first, so what you see is what hits, including swings that rise, fall or chop straight down; recovery, it drifts back to hovering.
- A parry (ParryAbility running): it guards in front of the pawn's chest, blade held flat across, edge out, for as long as the parry runs (`guard_forward`, `guard_height`).
- Dead: it drops to the ground beside the pawn, lying flat.

Combo swings alternate: after a swing it rests on the side where the swing ended, so the next swing starts from there. A swing ending on the left leaves it hovering at the pawn's left, the second swing then sweeps from left to right, and so on. A swing ending in the middle (a chop) leaves it where it was. After `return_seconds` with no swing it goes back to the right, round the front of the pawn rather than through it.

Visual only: it runs once per rendered frame, only reads the pawn, and changes nothing the game simulates. The swing's progress comes from the ability's state, which rolls back and reaches clients in snapshots, so a client sees other pawns' swings too, and the tick driver's interpolation fraction makes it smooth between ticks. With no display (a headless server or test), it builds nothing and never runs, since nothing can see it (RunEnvironment.runs_visuals). A host playing in a window still draws it.

### Settings and properties

- `sword_scene: PackedScene`: The sword to show, such as Kenney's weapon-sword.glb, with its blade along +Y and its grip at its origin. Empty: a plain box blade.
- `sword_scale: float` = `2.2`: How much bigger the sword is drawn. Kenney's is about 0.45 m long; 2.2 makes it about 1 m.
- `hover_side: float` = `0.8`: Where it hovers, from the pawn's feet: this far to the pawn's right, and this high, in metres.
- `hover_height: float` = `1.0`
- `bob_height: float` = `0.06`: How far it bobs up and down, in metres, and how many times a second.
- `bob_rate: float` = `1.1`
- `hover_lean_degrees: float` = `14.0`: How far the blade leans out from straight up, away from the pawn, in degrees.
- `swing_pivot_height: float` = `1.1`: How high the blade's pivot is above the pawn's feet during a swing, in metres: about the chest. The blade points from here through the spot the hit checks.
- `grip_distance: float` = `0.5`: How far out from that pivot the grip is during a swing, in metres.
- `windup_pull_back: float` = `0.2`: How far before the hit's start the windup pulls back, as a fraction of the sweep: 0.2 is a fifth of the sweep further back.
- `settle_seconds: float` = `0.12`: How long it takes to glide to its new pose when what it shows changes at once: a swing cancelled halfway, a new swing starting before the last one settled, or the pawn dying. The rest of the time it follows the swing exactly, with no lag, so even a fast chop is drawn where the hit is.
- `return_seconds: float` = `0.8`: Seconds with no swing before it goes back to the pawn's right from the side the last swing ended on.
- `side_change_seconds: float` = `0.35`: How long that trip round the front takes, in seconds.
- `guard_forward: float` = `0.6`: While a parry runs, how far in front of the pawn the guarding sword is, and how high, in metres.
- `guard_height: float` = `1.15`

### Functions

- `_target(facing: float) -> Transform3D`: Where the sword should be this frame, in world space: hovering, swinging or lying on the ground.

## ToyWaddle

`res://assets/scripts/visuals/ToyWaddle.gd`, extends [`Node3D`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node3d.html)

Makes a pawn's model move like a toy being played with: rocking, hopping, leaning into a dash and falling over when it dies.

The owner's toy look (pawn spec 8.12): it rocks from side to side and hops a little with each step instead of walking with legs, leans into a dash, tips back when knocked back, and falls over when it dies. Put it under the pawn's Visual/Model, with nothing else needed: it makes the model itself from `toy_scene`, and stands it on a coloured base like a figurine's, so teams can be told apart.

What it is and isn't:
- Visual only. It runs once per rendered frame, only reads the pawn, and changes nothing the game simulates, so it needs no rollback and works the same on the server, on a client predicting its own pawn, and on a client drawing other pawns.
- It moves only itself (this node). The pawn turns Visual/Model to face the way the pawn faces, and this sits inside that, so "forward" here is always the pawn's forward (-Z) and "side to side" is its left and right.
- Its origin is at the pawn's feet, so rocking and tipping over pivot on the ground, as a toy standing on a table does.

How fast it waddles comes from how fast the drawn model moves (Visual, smoothed between ticks), not from the pawn's velocity, so a pawn drawn from snapshots on a client waddles too. The step rate grows with speed: `steps_per_metre` steps for every metre.

The model: toy_scene is instanced as a child at `toy_scale` (turned round if `turn_model_round` is on). If it has an AnimationPlayer, the first frame of `pose_animation` holds the model in a still pose for the waddle to move.

With no display (a headless server or test), the figure isn't built and its per-frame waddle never runs, since nothing can see it (RunEnvironment.runs_visuals). A host playing in a window still draws it.

### Settings and properties

- `toy_scene: PackedScene`: The model to show, such as a Kenney character's .glb. Empty: nothing is made, and this only moves whatever children it already has.
- `toy_scale: float` = `2.2`: How much bigger the model is drawn. Kenney's mini characters are about 0.8 m tall; 2.2 makes them about the height of the pawn's 1.8 m capsule.
- `turn_model_round: bool` = `true`: On: the model is turned round 180 degrees, for a model that faces +Z, as Kenney's characters do (glTF's front is +Z). The pawn's forward is -Z.
- `pose_animation: StringName` = `&"idle"`: The animation whose first frame holds the model still, if it has an AnimationPlayer with one. Kenney's characters have "idle", whose first frame has the arms down ("static" holds them straight out).
- `stand_color: Color` = `Color(0.9, 0.75, 0.3, 1)`: The colour of the round base the figure stands on, like a toy figurine's. Fully clear (alpha 0): no base.
- `stand_radius: float` = `0.45`: The base's radius, in metres.
- `rock_degrees: float` = `10.0`: How far it rocks from side to side at full walking speed, in degrees each way.
- `hop_height: float` = `0.09`: How high each step's little hop is at full walking speed, in metres.
- `steps_per_metre: float` = `1.6`: Steps per metre walked. Each step is one rock to a side and one hop.
- `lean_degrees: float` = `6.0`: How far it leans forward while moving at full walking speed, in degrees.
- `walk_speed: float` = `5.0`: The speed counted as full walking speed, in metres per second, for the amounts above. Faster (sprinting) rocks and hops a little more, up to one and a half times.
- `breathe_height: float` = `0.015`: Standing still: how far it bobs up and down, in metres, and how many times a second.
- `breathe_rate: float` = `0.8`
- `dash_lean_degrees: float` = `28.0`: While dashing: how far it leans forward, in degrees.
- `knockback_tilt_degrees: float` = `22.0`: While being knocked back: how far it tips backward, in degrees.
- `air_tilt_degrees: float` = `8.0`: While off the ground: how far it tilts back, in degrees.
- `death_fall_degrees: float` = `90.0`: When it dies: how far it falls over onto its side, in degrees (90 is flat), and how fast it settles there.
- `ease_rate: float` = `12.0`: How quickly it eases toward a new lean or tilt: higher is snappier. Each frame it closes this fraction of the gap per second, roughly; 12 settles in about a quarter of a second.
